transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-23
Start: 11:00 UTC
Duration: ~46 min
Attendees: Samira Khan (Redwood AE), Diego Alvarez (Redwood SE), Priya Menon (Lyra Eng Manager), Marcus Cole (Lyra SRE), Leah Ortiz (Lyra Product)

Summary:
Brief: Weekly POC check-in focused on follow-up from yesterday's throttling incident and a planned load/play run. Actionable tuning items for retries, rate windows, and KV cache warmup. Agreement to run long-form test on dedicated pool and exchange security artifacts.

Topics:
- Recent 5xx spike and timeouts during morning test
- Rate-limiter behavior and retry budget settings
- KV cache warm state and cold-start penalties
- Dedicated pool vs hosted fallback routing tradeoffs
- Observability gaps: missing token-level traces for some requests

Action items (captured verbally, see metadata): Diego to run load test; Samira to share security docs; Marcus to dump rate-limiter config; Leah to finalize success criteria.

--- Transcript (timestamps approximate) ---
[00:00] Samira (Redwood): Okay hey everyone thanks for joining, I'm seeing five people, we'll give another minute then jump in.
[00:28] Priya (Lyra): Hey, thanks, yeah running a bit late this morning, sorry about that. We had an oncall earlier.
[00:35] Diego (Redwood SE): No worries. Quick agenda: run through what we saw in the AM test, go over proposed tuning for retries/rate windows, then schedule the longer run.
[00:50] Marcus (Lyra): Quick note — the 5xx spike was pretty bad for 8 minutes, and some user flows saw timeouts. We attached a heap of 502/504s in the logs.
[01:05] Leah (Lyra): For product, we care about tail latency and the error surface during peak load. If can avoid user-facing timeouts during retries that's ideal.
[01:18] Diego: Right. From the Redwood end we saw an increase in p95 token latency when the KV cache wasn't warm; that pushed requests into longer execution paths and bumped kernels. So two contributing things: cold K-V cash and a burst of parallel requests that tripped the per-tenant rate window. Sorry my transcription — K-V cash should be KV cache.
[01:40] Priya: Can you unpack the rate window bit? We use a 1s token window on our side and we thought that would be fine.
[01:50] Diego: Yeah, so we have two layers: application level rate-limiter and the serving side bucketing. When a big fanout happens — your client side fanout to multiple prompts — the aggregate tokens into that window can spike and cause the router to apply a short-term throttle. If retries are naive and immediate, they amplify the spike.
[02:15] Marcus: We did see retries fire from the client after the first 502, so that explains some of the amplification. What's the recommended backoff?
[02:24] Samira: Good question. For production we'd usually suggest an adaptive exponential backoff with jitter and a retry budget — e.g., max 3 retries, initial backoff 200-300ms, doubling, and a sliding window for the budget. Also Redwood has a retry-budget helper in the SDK but we can share config examples.
[02:46] Priya: Are there any server-side automatic fallbacks we should be aware of? Like if Dedicated is full does it fall back to hosted?
[02:55] Diego: Correct, routing policy can fallback to a compatible model on hosted or to a smaller quantized variant; but in your pilot you pinned a dedicated pool which should degrade instead of falling back unless you set policy to allow cross-pool fallbacks. For the POC we recommended pin to avoid silent model switches, but we can enable a controlled fallback for resilience.
[03:18] Leah: I think we want controlled fallback but only for non-sensitive flows; product will mark some endpoints as no-fallback.
[03:26] Diego: Makes sense. Also on KV cache — warmup is important. If your first burst after deployment hits cold cache, the per-request time is much higher. Warmup strategies: pre-seed prefixes for the common prompts, or run a short 5-10min warm traffic before production ramp.
[03:48] Marcus: Can Redwood expose cache hit metrics per tenant? We only saw aggregate metrics in the console.
[03:55] Samira: We can share a per-token cache hit rate curl example and add a dashboard tile for your account. I'll follow up with a screenshot.
[04:05] Priya: About the 5xxs — are those mostly our side or serving? The logs show a mix.
[04:12] Diego: Looking at the sample traces you shared, many were 502 with backend timeouts in the runtime. A smaller percentage were 5xx from overloaded decoders. We suspect the spike pushed the scheduler into backpressure, which then caused some connectors to time out.
[04:34] Marcus: Is there any quick tuning we can do on your side to reduce timeouts?
[04:40] Diego: Short term: increase the per-pool concurrency cap slightly during the test, and extend the RPC timeout by 200-300ms to tolerate a few stragglers. Longer term: KV warmup and smoothing ingest with a token-based token-bucket will help.
[04:59] Leah: Can we simulate the same pattern locally? Our stack makes 3 parallel prompts per end-user event, then a retry at 150ms. Should we change retry to 300ms for now?
[05:10] Samira: Yes, increasing initial backoff and adding jitter is low risk. Also set a global retry budget so clients stop retrying once the budget is spent.
[05:21] Priya: Diego, for the load test you proposed — what config do you want? RPS, token sizes, KV warm?
[05:30] Diego: We'll run a 30 minute sustained at 350 rps with a 30% burst window to emulate spikes. Payload distribution: 60% short (50-100 tokens), 30% med (200-400 tokens), 10% long (>800 tokens). We will pre-warm KV with the 60% short prompts and capture token-level latencies, queue times, and 5xx counts.
[05:58] Marcus: If you're going to bump concurrency, how do we avoid impacting other tenants?
[06:04] Diego: We'll run on your dedicated pool, and we'll coordinate the time window. Also we can temporarily reserve extra capacity just for the test if you approve.
[06:12] Leah: Cost question — how much will this dedicated test cost? We need a ballpark for approval.
[06:18] Samira: I'll put a rough estimate in the follow-up email: a 30m reserved test with the dedicated pool bump is about X credits — I'll get exact numbers.
[06:28] Priya: There's one other observation: some of our log traces lose the request-id mapping, so it's hard to correlate client retries to server 502s.
[06:37] Diego: That's an observability gap. We'll add request-id passthrough and a tracer tag that your instrumentation can pick up. Also we'll expose a sample query for token-level traces.
[06:48] Marcus: On security — are there controls for key rotation and HSM? We need to show this to our compliance team.
[06:55] Samira: Yes, Redwood Private has KMS/HSM integrations and key rotation. For hosted we provide encryption at rest and options to bring-your-own-key to our HSM through the enterprise plan. I'll attach the SOC2 and KMS notes.
[07:09] Priya: If we want to try controlled fallback to hosted for non-sensitive flows, any gotchas?
[07:15] Diego: Two gotchas: model parity and data residency. The hosted variant might be a slightly different quantization, so output could vary. Also if your data residency constraints require traffic to stay in your VPC/region, fallback might violate that unless we route to a regional hosted pool.
[07:33] Leah: Product-wise we'll mark three endpoints as no-fallback and allow fallback for analytics endpoints.
[07:40] Samira: Great. Next, I want to recap the plan so we're aligned. Diego will run the 30m load test on the dedicated pool, with KV warm, and share raw metrics and an annotated spreadsheet. Marcus will give rate-limiter config; Priya will try a client-side config change to ramp retry initial backoff to 300ms.
[08:03] Marcus: Also, on the runtime side we found one regression in our test that aligned with the last runtime kernel update. Diego, can you flag the kernel selection logs?
[08:13] Diego: Yep, I'll include kernel selection traces and sequence length distribution in the test artifacts.
[08:20] Priya: For the test window, can we do it on Monday morning? Our traffic pattern is similar then.
[08:26] Samira: Monday morning UTC works for Redwood too. I'll propose a 09:00 UTC slot in the calendar.
[08:31] Leah: I'll update the success criteria doc today and attach it to the drive.
[08:36] Diego: One more note — if you choose to enable controlled fallback, we recommend a staged rollout: enable for 10% traffic, monitor errors/latency for 1 hour, then expand. Don't open fallback to 100% at once.
[08:50] Marcus: Good call.
[08:54] Samira: Anything else?
[08:58] Priya: Can you also share a sample exponential backoff snippet for our client SDK? We have custom clients in Node and Python.
[09:05] Diego: Yes I'll paste code snippets and config.
[09:09] Samira: Alright thanks everyone. We'll follow through on the action items and share the test results + security docs.
[09:17] Leah: Thanks all.
[09:20] Meeting end.

Notes: transcript contains occasional auto-caption errors (KV cash, sam-el) — corrected inline. Some speaker attribution may be approximate.
